label: Walking skeleton S1 and S2: runs as background jobs streamed over SSE (#87), and the studio wiring (#90)
decisions: Track 2 (PR 14a) ran in a second herdr pane with its own worktree and session (Laurie)
Run progress streams over SSE, with the run detached from the connection (option B) (Laurie)
Run state is written by a scoped Postgres role through guarded functions; no MCP server; an ADR is held back while this is a POC, recorded in docs/decision-records/poc-design-notes.md (Laurie)
Append-only run_events log; SSE replays after Last-Event-ID, polls the cursor, and answers 204 to a client holding the final event (mine, from the robust-pattern question)
dispatch_run is the in-process seam that the NFR-02 worker pool replaces (mine)
The run_node_metrics foreign key to runs is deferred; it is a retention call (mine, flagged)
A run starts from an explicit button, the page shows the photograph, and 'Try again' appears only after a failure (Laurie; the retry is mine, flagged)
The studio validates each SSE event with Zod on the server and re-frames it; RunResult and RunFailure move into the shared schemas with parity fixtures (mine)
The studio size-limit is raised from 300 kB to 500 kB (Laurie)
peekAccessToken: a read-only token peek for Server Components (from review)
#88 is P2 (Laurie); #91, token refresh, is P2 (mine, delegated)

retro.went_well: Both slices were checked end to end against the real local stack before shipping. S1 ran in-process with real auth, the Postgres run log and PostgREST reads. S2 ran in a headless browser through the real Next server, which proved the SSE was not buffered. Design calls were put as side-by-side options, and the SSE question became a short write-up of the standard pattern, which Laurie then chose. Every outward write was read back, including PR bodies, review replies and comment bodies.
retro.improve: On #87 my resolve loop closed Greptile's own unaddressed threads along with mine, and I had to reopen them. Greptile's three findings on #90 were all reachable from code I could have read first: getAccessToken writes a cookie, fetch can reject, and releaseLock does not cancel. I stated that operations holds service_role from a migration comment, without checking newer decisions. I also wrote the 'reviewed by @lsr-explore' footer before noticing it was untrue, and caught it before posting.
retro.tooling_suggestion: Before a resolve step, filter threads to ones I posted or replied to. Before calling an auth helper from a new context (a Server Component, a background task), read what it writes. Make `pnpm size` build first, or warn when .next is older than the source; it silently measured a day-old build.
